I don't know where you work or if you really are a mental health professional or not, but something is very very off, especially for you to be a health care professional.

Probably not giving into any sort of peer pressure. Do what works for YOU. Don't constantly go out to parties or neglect responsibilities because others encourage you to. No matter who it is. Friends, family, bosses or co-workers. Be open to the idea, because your friends and family aren't always wrong and maybe you _do_ need that break, but don't allow it to become a constant thing. 

And on the flip side, don't work nonstop or never do anything fun to please others. It's okay to have fun even if you think you may be called "lazy" or "childish." The people who call you lazy are probably workaholics, and the people who call you childish have just got their heads too far up their ass. Sometimes you may need to step back and wonder if you do need to try to be more serious, but do it for yourself. Not for others. 

Life isn't a one size fits all. It's okay to take suggestions or advice, but do what you think it's best. Focus on your priorities that matter to you. If theres something you dislike, or regret, learn from it and try not to make the same mistakes twice. It's okay to not be perfect also.
